transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess the main thing is I feel like I’m always up and moving. Even on a quiet day, I’ll be bouncing from the garden club list to my knitting bag to travel papers, and I haven’t really finished any one thing before I’m on to the next.
Has this feeling of being constantly restless and unable to finish tasks been present since you were a child, or is this a new change that started more recently?

No, it’s not really new. Even back in grade school, I remember teachers telling my mother I was bright, but scattered. I’d lose papers, talk when I wasn’t supposed to, and I’d be wiggling around in my seat before I ever finished my work.
Right now, would you say these patterns of restlessness and difficulty finishing tasks are causing problems for you in more than one area of your life—like at home, at work, or in your relationships?

Yes. It’s causing strain at home with my husband, and also at the community center where I volunteer. People can’t really count on me to keep plans straight unless someone checks behind me, and that’s been upsetting.
Do you often find yourself interrupting conversations, blurting out responses before someone finishes speaking, or having trouble waiting your turn in lines or discussions?

Yes, I do. My husband tells me I cut him off before he’s finished talking. And in group planning, I’ll jump in because I’m worried if I don’t say it right then, I’ll lose the thought. I don’t mean to be rude, but it comes out that way sometimes.
Thinking back to before you were about 12 years old, can you tell me if these same kinds of symptoms—like being easily distracted, fidgety, or impulsive—were noticeably present at that age?

Yes, it was there back then. In grade school my teachers would tell my mother I was bright, but scattered. I was always losing papers, talking out of turn, and wiggling around in my seat before I’d finish my work.

Have you ever had distinct periods lasting several days or more where you felt unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, and had racing thoughts—different from your usual baseline?
I don’t think so. I mean, I have times where I’m restless or keyed up, but not several days where I feel euphoric or need hardly any sleep. Nothing that feels that different from my usual self.
Do you currently use caffeine, nicotine, alcohol, or any other substances or medications that might make you feel more restless or wired?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything in particular that makes me feel more wired, but I’d have to think about it.
Do you often experience excessive worry or nervousness about various things that's hard to control, separate from the restlessness we've discussed?
I’m not really sure. I do worry about things sometimes, but I don’t know that I’d call it excessive or separate from the restlessness. It’s not something I’ve clearly noticed as its own problem.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a lifelong pattern (since grade school, confirmed onset prior to age 12) of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity including distractibility, disorganization, fidgeting/restlessness, interrupting others, and difficulty waiting turn. These symptoms have persisted into adulthood and cause impairment in multiple settings (marital relationship and volunteer work). Bipolar disorder was ruled out as the patient denied distinct episodes of elevated/irritable mood with decreased need for sleep. Generalized anxiety was considered but the patient did not endorse excessive, uncontrollable worry distinct from the restlessness. The clinical picture is most consistent with ADHD, combined presentation (F90.0).
